children: Hampered by bad weather and air traffic control issues, JetBlue
faced disruptions  this summer that undermined the total number of seats that were available to sell to passengers.
In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, JetBlue

revised its capacity estimates for the third quarter to reflect a 40% increase in severe airport weather days across the National Airspace System and air traffic control-related cancellations that nearly doubled. These disruptions impacted the carrier’s operational results and raised its costs per available seat mile (CASM) excluding fuel.

Accordingly, the airline now expects CASM ex-fuel to increase by 6% to 8% from an earlier estimate of up 2.5% to 4.5% and lowered its available seat miles (ASM) estimate for the third quarter to 1.5% to 3.5% from an earlier estimate of ASM growth of 3% to 6%.

However, strong underlying demand for air travel, a constructive pricing environment, and “targeted commercial actions” allowed for a more favorable revenue outlook for the third quarter, offsetting some of the pressure from higher fuel and operational costs.
now expects revenue per available seat mile (RASM) to increase by 17% to 20% from a prior estimate of up 12.5% to 16.5%.
The airline also lowered its outlook for capital expenditures to ~$275M from ~$300M.
Shares are modestly lower in Thursday’s open, with pressure on the travel industry exacerbated by another spike in oil futures.

title: JetBlue lowers Q3 capacity outlook on summer disruptions but raises RASM outlook
